messages:
Grace Li: Need helpI have joint custody of my teen and want to add them to my Redwood plan. Ex says theyll keep them on their plan for now but might drop coverage midyear. What docs do you need if I need to switch primary later?

Sam (People Ops): Short answer: for a QLE to change primary coverage (gain/loss of other coverage) we usually need proof of the other plan's loss. For custody-specific asks, carriers sometimes request custody/court orders only if the dependent was NOT previously covered by you.

Grace Li: Kid was on my plan at hire but then moved to exs plan last year. If they lose that coverage midyear, will carrier accept my request to re-add without custody papers?

Cam (Benefits): If your child has previously been enrolled on your plan and the QLE is loss of other coverage, carriers typically focus on proof of the loss (COBRA notice, termination letter). If the child was never enrolled under your subscriber record, then we may need proof of relationship (birth cert) and possibly custody docs if the carrier flags it.

Grace Li: What counts as a valid "proof of loss"? The ex says they were offered COBRA but haven't returned paperwork.

Cam (Benefits): Acceptable docs: carrier termination letter with effective date, COBRA election notice showing the option to continue and the effective date of loss of active employer coverage, or an HR/benefits confirmation email from their employer. A screenshot is ok if it includes header, employer name and dates.

Grace Li: If the ex delays paperwork, is there a way to provisionally add my child so I'm not left without coverage?

Sam (People Ops): We can open a case and request carrier to allow retroactive enrollment if you submit within the carrier's QLE window (usually 30-60 days). Carriers vary: some allow provisional enrollment pending docs, others require the proof before activation. We'll ask, but no guarantees.

Grace Li: Suppose carrier says they need custody docs. I have a parenting plan PDF with signatures but it's redacted. Will that work?

Cam (Benefits): A parenting plan, custody order, or court-issued document is what carriers look for. It must show legal custody arrangements and ideally the child's name and dates. Redactions are fine for sensitive info as long as the required elements (names, custody terms) are visible. If the carrier rejects, we'll escalate to our broker/rep.

Grace Li: Any privacy concerns about sending custody docs? Can I send only whats necessary?

Sam (People Ops): Yes, we only need the relevant page(s). Send docs via encrypted email or the secure HR portal. Email benefits@redwood.com with subject "QLE - add dependent - custody docs" and in the body note any redactions. We store docs in the secure HR system and limit access.

Grace Li: Does adding midyear affect my HSA eligibility? Kid's coverage moving between HDHP/PPO could matter right?

Cam (Benefits): Good point. If you enroll the child in a non-HDHP plan through you, it could impact HSA contributions. For example, if your spouse's plan becomes primary and is non-HDHP, you could lose HSA eligibility. We'll flag payroll and HSA admin when processing. If HSA eligibility changes midyear, you'll need to coordinate contributions and potential distribution/rollover rules with payroll and Fidelity/Vendor.

Grace Li: Timeline: if the exs plan ends Aug 15 and I email docs Aug 20, when might coverage start?

Cam (Benefits): If submitted within carrier window and carrier approves, effective date is often the date of loss (Aug 15). If carrier requires a next-month effective date, they might set Sep 1. We'll confirm the effective date in our case response. Payroll proration/retro credits handled after enrollment is processed.

Grace Li: Okay sending termination letter now. Thanks.

benefits-bot: Reminder: QLE docs should be submitted within carrier windows (usually 30-60 days). Open enrollment runs Nov 1- Nov 15. Changes made during open enrollment take effect Jan 1.

Grace Li: Appreciate it :slightly_smiling_face:
